reviews.comment: He's genuinely an awesome person, but not so great of a teacher. Lost a lot of weight from the stress, so take him if you're on a weight loss journey ig. Made MATH 152 and PHYS 206 look easy. Seems like only people with a strong chem background enjoyed him, so take that as you will.

Dr. Han's lectures are entirely disorganized and difficult to follow because his lecture style is fairly scattered and he scribbles at seemingly random when doing example problems. Additionally, maybe 40% of the example problems he worked required correction from a student in the class. He doesn't listen to feedback or his students.

Dr.Han is a very caring prof and truly enjoys teaching chemistry. However thats all he has going for him. His accent is very thick and his slides are super disorganized making class difficult to follow. I spent the majority of my time teaching myself the material instead of studying for other classes. Take someone else if you can.

The CHEM318 lab was very well ran by Dr. Han. Although it's very TA-dependent, he was very accessible and cared about our learning during the labs. Weekly lab reports are graded very fairly and there's a rubic provided. Final and quizzes were very easy and just based on the lab readings and calculations. Overall great choice just time consuming.

Genuinely the hate on Dr. Han is forced. I took him this semester and felt that his class was very fair compared to these other reviews. He gives out extra credit, has homework that has plenty attempts, and I-clicker points will help you. His lectures are fine, they are not the best but not the worst. Overall I think he was a nice and caring prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Han is a great person and cares a lot about his students. This is already a pretty difficult course, so it isn't easy to gauge professors as well. Although his lectures aren't very easy to understand I'd say he prepares you well for the tests. I did the bare minimum for the class and still pulled out with a B. Just show up!

Went from an A in chem119 to a D in chem120. Not a bad guy but cannot teach. Went to other prof office hours and learned much more from them in a short time than I ever did for Han. Exams are most of your grade, and while not super hard, he doesn't teach you enough to be prepared. Doesn't curve. It's not you or the course, he just cannot teach.

Professor Han was honestly not so bad. After reading the reviews, I was nervous. At first, his accent was a little confusing, but honestly, I got used to it really fast and realized he's a great lecturer and he really cares for his students. His exams aren't hard if you just do the practice questions he gives, which are similar to the exams.

he seems like a nice guy, but he can't lecture. i spent lecture time teaching myself after the first few weeks, since his explanations only confused me more. homework is deceptively easy, and quizzes are incredibly hard; exams are ok. also, all other gen chem 2 profs curve except him (allegedly). we get a tiny bit of extra credit tho!
dropped this class, hes nice but his lectures didn't do it for me and i was failing miserably

Only got an A in the class because I took AP Chem my senior year. If you don't have a good or strong background knowledge of chemistry I would avoid him. Hard to understand and for the things I didn't know or forgot, I had to self teach myself. Few quizzes, not that much homework, and a decent bit of extra credit. Definitely better options.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take him if you don't have to... exams are also not like his reviews.

The worst professor I've ever had. Lecture isn't helpful, he doesn't go through the entire practice problems, blames the students if they fail, and his office hours don't help either. He has an accent and mumbles so you can't understand him. Take this class with anyone else. And if not, prepare to learn all the content on your own.

Dr. Han is extremely nice and rly accessible outside of class! He provides practice questions that are decently similar to the actual exam. It is better to learn from him privately in his office than to take notes in lecture, because he can get a little confusing during his lectures. Overall great guy, great one one one tutor, and an OK lecturer.

I took AP chem and thats the only reason I got an A in this class. Seems like a really nice guy, his accent just makes it really hard to pay attention in class and it sometimes gives me a headache trying to focus. STUDY LECTURE SLIDES and ICLICKER! practice exams and HW too easy compared to exam, try your best on quizzes. Gives extra credit tho.

Makes his quizzes and exams harder on purpose and has to curve the grades at the end of the semester. He has an accent and he mutters so its impossible to understand him half the time. Has caused me to do bad on other tests cause of how much I have to focus on this class. Cant really think of any pros avoid at all costs unless you want to fall

Nowhere near as bad as people are making him out to be; he teaches fine and he gladly answers questions. The class is so easy that it literally doesn't matter who you get, he provides all info and responds to emails fast so just study if you don't get it

Dr. Han is very nice, but he has a very strong Korean accent and is super hard to understand. His quizzes are hard, and his exams aren't too hard. There wasn't much homework. Other than his accent, his lectures are great. I recommend choosing a different professor if you aren't good at chemistry, but if you are good at chemistry, then Han is great.
His lectures are very superficial and he commonly makes mistakes during example problems that students have to spend minutes correcting him on.

Take anyone else. His lectures are impossible to follow and at most go over the absolute basics, but attendance is mandatory for iClicker. His homework is also super basic, so you'll need to do extensive studying to pass his quizzes and exams. Chem is bad enough already, and Han just makes it even more unbearable.
Very thick accent

I could write a book on how many things I would rather do than sit in a lecture hall with THE Sungyub Han ever again. He is genuinely one of the sweetest profs you will ever meet, but I can confidently say I learned nothing from him. Except the gospel.

Dr. Han has a pretty thick accent that may make him hard to understand, but he is a very caring professor who wants you to succeed. However, homework in his class is deceptively easy and does not prepare you well for his quizzes and exams. He also has a tendency to make lots of mistakes in lectures. To do well, you have to ready the textbook.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take him unless you're a genius at Chemistry. He's a very nice guy, so accesible outside of office hours and cares but he cannot lecture. I do not mind his accent but he mumbles and speaks quietly often and his handwriting is not good at all and when dealing with chemistry that's a huge killer. His practice exams were unlike the real exam.

Don't listen to the various negative reviews for Dr. Han - he is sincere, committed, and truly has a passion for chemistry. Although some of his quizzes and tests seem difficult, everything you need to know will be listed in his presentation or iClicker Questions.

He was a really nice person, but it was tough to understand the concepts as they were taught at a very fast pace. Many students struggled in this class, especially those who hadn't taken AP CHEM. The lectures are very superficial and did not help me grasp chemistry concepts
Speaks somewhat quietly and tends to speed over concepts during lectures. Read the textbook before/during lectures, do the iclicker questions in advance.

This is my first rating because it is RIDICULOUS how you simply don't learn ANYTHING in class. No matter who your prof is classes can behard normal but Doctor Han, as nice as he is, simply can't teach. You will not learn in during lecture. id go with other profs who actually teach during class because it simply saves you time. TRUST ME!!!!!!!!!!!

This professor has an accent that makes him hard to understand at times, but he cares a lot about his students and is very willing to help you out when you need it. Go to his office hours and ask a lot of questions, take advantage of all of your resources and you'll do fine.

Dr.Han was the most caring professor I had this semester. He has an accent thats slightly hard to understand, but you get used to it fairly quick. The first exam was hard, so he made the second exam easier and gave extra practice problems. He reviewed in class when we were struggling and was always available for office hours. Chem107 is just hard.

Professor Han is a great person and wants his students to succeed, however his lectures are straight from the slides with no post lecture notes, often would make mistakes in problem comprehension and while quizzes/ exams weren't extremely difficult they often had questions mentioned once on a slides he glossed over.

super nice guy that always tried to make time for students outside of class but not a great lecturer. has an accent that makes it hard to understand and also goes super fast so its easy to get lost if you miss one thing. also js randomly starts talking about the bible during class or some other random stories instead of teaching chemistry.

Dr. Han is a really nice person and coveys a love for chemistry, but his class is unnecessarily hard. His homeworks are really easy which totally baits you for the impossible quizzes. His practice exams are also much easier than the actual exams themselves so you have to do everything yourself in this class just to survive.

His accent was very hard for me to understand and often times the lecture material had no correlation to the quizzes or exams. The HW is easy, but they have no resemblance to the quizzes or test. The practice test that he gave were 3X easier than the actual test. I had to teach myself chem, he's an ok guy but that doesn't mean he can teach.

Professor Han is honestly such a nice and wholesome guy. His very strong accent makes it so difficult to understand him so you probably won't learn very much during the lectures. He does iclicker every single lecture so you can't really skip. I also felt like he made his tests harder than other profs. He also gets side tracked easily.

Professor Han is a fantastic guy. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. HOWEVER, he can't teach and you will have to learn the material outside of lecture. I would take another prof if you can, ETAM is already stressful enough.

Chemistry itself is hard. Dr. Han has an accent and if you're not paying attention, you will get lost. IMO the quizzes were harder than the tests. He does provide videos over the lecture material (done by a different professor) which were very useful, especially if you skipped class. Not the worst ever, but there are definitely better options.

Professor Han was a great leader in the lecture hall, offering words of encouragement at every turn. I loved having him as someone who was there if needed; however, this class was difficult as Professor Han sometimes is hard to understand. He does offer a lot of resources and material if you care enough to get a good grade, but it is hard.

Complete scam of a course. Lectures are impossible to understand and polling/homework are 10x easier than the quizzes and exams. But not like you can just skip and use that hour to study the actually important stuff because attendance is 10% of your grade. He's a nice guy, but that doesn't compensate for the genuinely awful teaching quality.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy, but you won't learn much from his lectures. Attendance is mandatory and he has a bit of an accent but it's not impossible to understand. Overall, you will need to work extremely hard outside of class to learn the material and I only managed to scrape an A at the very end. He won't round up your grade either.

He is a really nice guy but it is very hard to understand him. He rushes through lecture and does Iclicker questions on the board. Unfortunately none of the questions are anything like what is on exams and quizzes. Gives practice questions for exams but they are 3x easier than what's actually on the exams. Avoid if possible

Really nice guy, but hard to understand. Breezes through content and doesn't do a good enough job explaining difficult concepts. The quizzes were extremely hard compared to the homeworks but the tests were doable. Be prepared to study extremely hard and learn everything from khan academy/organic chemistry tutor.

You can't understand him, but one of the nicest teacher I have ever had. He is very understanding and helpful at office hours but the lecture room was very difficult to understand what he was saying. Quizzes are the hardest exams are a little easier but still hard. If you put in a good amount of work you should be fine.

Cannot teach, ignores requests for clarification unless you show up to his office hours, where he admittedly does try to help, but falls short. Some examples of how other professors are better for chem are that they give relevant practices to their tests (Han does not) and actually helps you prepare for exams. Hans class has lowest avgs for this.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Han is a kind person, but not good at teaching. Lectures are literally just summaries, and homework is incredibly easy which makes it hard to know what to study for. The quizzes test on stuff that was not taught in class. Exams were easier than quizzes. If you take this professor, get ready to have to teach yourself.

He can't teach. The accent is really hard to understand and he keeps on talking and teaching new concepts in every word he says, meaning if you zone out 5 minutes you will miss like 3 chapters worth information but then when you sit and listen to him it feels like eternity. I guess this class is an example of Einstein's relativity.

Han is a really kind and caring professor, but is not very good at teaching chemistry. He has a thick accent and terrible handwriting during lectures. I literally showed up to lectures only to do the iClicker and had to teach everything to myself at home. Homeworks are incredibly easy, while quizzes are difficult, and the exams were alright.

Professor Han cares a lot about his students, but is simply terrible at teaching. His accent is very thick, his handwriting is impossible to read, and during the lectures he skims over the content that is emphasized on his extremely difficult quizzes. His office hours can be helpful for homework and content, but I would not recommend taking him.

The language barrier is insane, at some point throughout the semester I stopped attending lecture and watched his zoom recording instead just because it was a little easier to understand him. If you are not good at chemistry or major is not chemistry related take another professor.

If you are not good at/new to chemistry, probably take another professor. Dr Han is a kind and caring professor, but he is hard to understand, especially during the lecture. The iClicker assignments are necessary, meaning attending class is necessary, but you can miss some. Easy hw, HARD quizzes, and alright exams. You HAVE to spend time studying.

If you are new to chem, I strongly suggest any of the other professors. He consistently has the lowest averages on quizzes and tests compared to other professors. While I feel he actually cares about you succeeding, he can't really help you get there. He has a very strong accent and awful handwriting.

Extremely hard to understand accent. In-class lecture slides consist of super-easy questions, homework is pretty easy, and quizzes are completely different than anything you are taught. Hardest things ever compared to rest of class. It's literally only this teacher. SWITCH AT ALL COSTS! QUIZZES BTHO YOU! DO NOT GIVE TENURE! 0/10 great person though

VERY nice man. However, it is quite difficult to learn from him. The quizzes in the class are very hard but the tests are pretty easy if you study using his materials. Also, he uses iclicker and attendance is required.

I always read rate my professor, making sure my prof selections and class selections are not going to be the reason why I get a bad grade. Most of the time when I see someone complain about a class or a prof. I assume it is about the person themselves because they did not put in the work. However Han is a great person but he simply CANNOT TEACH.

I think he cares alot and is a good person, but he was extremely hard to understand in class, and his homework always was bugging online and never prepared me for any quiz or exam. Good luck, I only got a good grade because I knew other people in my class that had already taken chemistry in high school.

Tests are okay but quizzes are pretty horrible. Honestly, not that bad if you are comfortable with the content in general or have taken Chem before. His quizzes are overly difficult and lecture material usually isn't thorough enough to cover everything on the quiz. You definitely can get an A with a modest amount of effort, class still sucks tho.

Dr. Han is a very nice person, but he's not a good professor. His accent is unintelligible, his handwriting is hard to read, as he spends at least 5 minutes of each class talking about God instead of chemistry. Attendance is mandatory via iClicker and unlike other professors  the iClicker lecture questions are for a grade and not extra credit.

Dr Han's lectures are not good and they do not prep you.
He is very quiet, sometimes his accent is very hard to follow, he does not explain the Iclicker questions well, his office hours he doesn't really explain questions well

also he goes on funny rants sometimes that aren't intended to be funny like when he talked about legos or spraying lizards

Watch Professor Pellois's review videos that he links in each chapter module. They're the only way you'll do well in the course, because it's impossible to learn anything during his lectures, which don't prepare you at all for the quizzes/exams.

General chemistry should not be this difficult, all of these concepts just require correct guidance, and his language barrier, useless homework, and very difficult quizzes, make this class unnecessarily hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
After an entire semester of attending his lectures, I still can barely understand what he is saying and still cannot read his god awful hand writing. 

His quizzes and tests are both definitively harder than other professors despite him giving us easier homework.

He also yaps about finding God for 15 minutes every lecture.........

Do not take him

Unfortunately, even though Dr. Han is a very approachable and friendly professor. It is generally hard to read his hand writing and understand what he says during lectures sometimes. The quizzes that he provides are also difficult and more thorough than his home works and lectures and will effect your grade heavily.

He's a genuinely great person, but he can be pretty hard to understand at times. His quizzes are notoriously difficult, and he's not exactly the strongest lecturer. On top of that, the homework is so easy that it's hard to tell what you actually need to study, which just adds to the confusion.
Bad lectures

If you have a chance to switch professors, do it. He is difficult to understand due to his accent. He is also very religious and spends 10 mins a lecture talking about how you should find truth in god. THE QUIZZES ARE TERRIBLE, and will destroy your grade. Reach out to other kids in other classes for their homework as his is very easy and unhelpful

If your new to chemistry I would not recommend taking this professor, the professor seemed like a great guy but lectures felt like word scramble when trying to actually understand. Quizzes are unbelievably harder then homeworks. If you must take this class I would not settle for a 8am.

Don't take him if you're just trying to get a high grade. 90% of his lecture you can't understand, and his quizzes (which are nothing like what he goes over in lecture) will literally assassinate your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Han is a great guy . You can tell he wants you to succeed. That being said he is a little hard to understand. Also his quizzes are nothing like the homework and lectures. If you don't study outside of class or don't get a tutor your probably not going to pass. I had already taken dual credit chemistry and still almost failed the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Han is a great person and he truly cares about his students. He can be hard to understand at times but it is so easy to tell how much he wants us to succeed. As long as you put in the effort, go to office hours, and watch the lecture videos posted on modules you should do good. This class is just designed to be hard no matter who you have.

Nice guy but not great at actually teaching. Breezes through concepts during lecture that he ends up testing heavy on, and fails to explain the harder stuff in an understandable way. Quizzes/exams are also way harder than polling questions he gives in class. Overall, just be prepared to get hard-carried by Dr. B and OCT.

He's nice and responsive on email, but unfortunately very difficult to understand in lecture. What you could comprehend in lecture barely skims the surface of what you need to know for the quizzes and tests. It's an unnecessary struggle in his class for something that simply requires clear guidance.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a decent professor, but very difficult to understand due to a heavy accent. Lectures were very surface level in comparison to the quizzes and tests. You will have to study and attend tutoring sessions to succeed in his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things
